title: FSSAI Confines Bisleri Action to One Goa Batch; Company Says Stock Is Gone
excerpt: The regulator clarified that only Batch GO 270 was found non-compliant and barred from sale. Bisleri says no stock of the batch remains, all 143 plants are running, and it disputes the PAH findings.
body:
• The FSSAI clarified on Monday, November 23, 2026, that only one sample from one Bisleri batch, GO 270, made at the company's Goa plant, was found non-compliant, and that a sale prohibition covers that batch alone.
  • On referral re-testing, bromate was below the limit of quantification and within the 0.01 mg/l limit, while PAH was detected at 0.144 micrograms per litre; under FSS Rule 2.4.6 the referral laboratory's report is final.
  • Bisleri said on Tuesday that no stock of batch GO 270 remains in the market, all 143 of its plants are operational, and it disputes the PAH findings, having sought a re-test in February 2026.
  • For shoppers: the order is batch-specific, not a brand ban or a nationwide recall. The affected batch was manufactured in Goa on September 27, 2025.

India's food safety regulator has narrowed its Bisleri action to a single batch, and the company says that batch is no longer on sale. In a clarification issued on Monday, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) confirmed that only one sample from one batch, Batch No. GO 270, at Bisleri's Goa plant was found non-compliant, and that its order prohibiting sale applies to that batch alone, ANI reported.

The clarification follows the FSSAI's sanction of prosecution against Bisleri International, reported over the weekend. The regulator's statement was aimed at the scope of the case: one sample, one batch, one plant.

What the two lab reports found

The sample, collected from Bisleri's plant at Verna Electronic City, Verna, Salcete, in South Goa, was first tested by a primary laboratory, Envirocare Labs in Mumbai. That report recorded bromates at 0.012 mg/l, above the 0.01 mg/l limit in the Food Safety and Standards Regulations, while polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH) were detected below 0.00001 mg/l and sent for further examination.

On Bisleri's appeal, the referral laboratory, NFL in Navi Mumbai, found PAH at 0.000144 mg/l (0.144 micrograms per litre), while bromates were below the limit of quantification and within the 0.01 mg/l limit. Under FSS Rule 2.4.6, the referral laboratory's report is final when a food business operator appeals. Following that report, the FSSAI issued the sale prohibition for Batch GO 270 under Section 36(3) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, and directed the company to carry out a root cause analysis.

Bisleri's response

Bisleri said on Tuesday that the sale prohibition applies only to Batch GO 270, manufactured in Goa on September 27, 2025, and that no stocks of the batch are in the market currently. The company, which says it produces more than 50,000 batches a year, said the FSSAI had "categorically and conclusively clarified on 23 November 2026 that bromates were found below permissible limit on re-testing of the batch (GO 270) sample."

On the PAH finding, Bisleri said one re-tested sample reported PAHs at 0.144 micrograms per litre while another sample from the same batch cleared all parameters, and that because of these discrepancies it had requested PAH re-testing in February this year. It said there have been no adverse PAH findings in any sample tested by the FSSAI across its plants since then, that its Goa plant received no direction to suspend operations, and that samples from subsequent production met all applicable FSSAI standards. The company said it would continue to cooperate with the FSSAI and defend its position in any proceedings.

What this means if you buy Bisleri

The regulator's order does not ban the Bisleri brand, shut the Goa plant or recall other batches. It covers Batch GO 270, produced on September 27, 2025, which the company says is no longer in the market. The prosecution sanction is a decision to prosecute, not a court verdict; the case will now turn on the referral laboratory's findings, which the rules treat as final.
